approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would change the Biosecurity Act 2015 to make biosecurity operations more efficient and effective.

It would require travellers to provide biosecurity information at set times and in set ways, such as through the digital Australia Travel Declaration, and would require a Notice of Intention before certain decisions on approved arrangements.
The obligation for travellers mirrors the existing power in section 196 of the Act to require information from those entering Australia by aircraft or vessel.
Require travellers to provide biosecurity information or documents at prescribed times and in prescribed manners.
Require a Notice of Intention before refusing an application for approving or varying an approved arrangement under Chapter 7 of the Act.
Remove the term 'relevant information' from section 568 of the Act.
Travellers entering Australia by aircraft or vessel, and biosecurity industry participants seeking approved arrangements.

Declared that specified telecommunications, therapeutic goods, biosecurity, and wine legislation would stand referred to the Federation Chamber, either immediately or following adjournment of second-reading debates, unless otherwise ordered.

Supported the Biosecurity Amendment (Improving Operational Efficiency) Bill 2026, which would introduce a digital Australian travel declaration alongside the paper card, retain alternatives for travellers without suitable devices, and add procedural safeguards for biosecurity arrangements. Argued that border modernisation must be matched by sustained federal support for controlling invasive species affecting agriculture and biodiversity.

Supported the Biosecurity Amendment (Improving Operational Efficiency) Bill 2026, which would enable digital Australia travel declarations, establish procedural fairness for approved arrangements and correct a drafting issue, while maintaining biosecurity standards; the bill passed its second reading and was reported without amendment.
